tagline.text: A beginner-friendly hike near Manila with sea-of-clouds dawns and the Noah's Ark ridge

location.label: Location
location.text: Sitio Maysawa, Barangay Cuyambay, Tanay, Rizal, inside the Fresno Agro-Forestry Eco-Tourist Campsite

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,200~1,500 (per person for a day trip from Manila)

children.text: Mount Kulis is a low mountain of about 620 m inside a private campsite in Tanay, Rizal. Leave Manila in the early morning, catch the sunrise and the sea of clouds, walk past Noah's Ark and the Spider Web viewpoint, and be back down before lunch. It is a good route for beginners.
Mount Kulis lies in Sitio Maysawa, on the boundary of Barangay Cuyambay and Barangay Laiban in Tanay, Rizal. Its summit is commonly given as about
, and the neighboring Sambong Peak is about

. The whole mountain sits within the private Fresno Agro-Forestry and Eco-Tourist Campsite, so you register at the entrance and hike with a guide. It is roughly 2.5 to 3 hours by road from central Manila and is popular as a sunrise hike.

The appeal is the scenery, not the height. In the early morning, clouds can settle toward the Sierra Madre range, and the rock viewpoint called Noah's Ark, the net-shaped Spider Web viewpoint, and the heart-shaped Sambong Peak have become well-known photo spots along the ridge. From the summit you can see toward the Sierra Madre and Laguna de Bay. The sea of clouds is usually visible only until about
, so everyone hurries up in the dark. Most visitors arrive before dawn, climb the ridge with a headlamp, take photos at sunrise, and head down before the morning sun gets hot.

There are two main routes. Camp A is the ridge route linking the summit, Noah's Ark, the Spider Web, and Sambong Peak. Camp B descends toward the river valley to reach the hanging bridge, Lion House Falls, and more. Camp A alone is a light outing, and doing both usually takes
3–5 hours
. Several blogs rate the difficulty at 2 to 3 out of 9, which is manageable for beginners, but the red clay trail gets slippery in the rainy season.

One planning tip: Mount Kulis is not a one-stop day on its own, and it fits well at the start of a Rizal outing near Manila. Many people finish the hike early in the morning and then add a waterfall or the wind farm in Tanay that afternoon. Because you start so early, pace your energy. Also note that this is a private campsite, not a national park. Fees, rules, and whether it is open are up to the operator. Blogs quote different entrance fees, so treat every amount in this article as approximate and check the latest notice on the Fresno campsite's Facebook page or on site before you go.
From the summit and the Noah's Ark ridge you may see a sea of clouds at dawn. It usually disperses before
, so aim to be on the ridge before
. On overcast days there may be no sea of clouds.
A rock viewpoint jutting out at the end of the red-dirt ridge, and the most photographed spot on Mount Kulis. On weekends the photo queue can reach
10–30 minutes
or more.
A net-shaped lookout on the ridge with a thrilling open view below. If you are afraid of heights, follow your guide's instructions and go up one person at a time.
A peak of about
reached by a short, easy climb from Noah's Ark. The walk up is said to take about
10 minutes
. It is also called Heart Peak.
The summit shelter is described as a new house built after the original hut was destroyed by Typhoon Ulysses in November 2020. From the registration area it is a short walk of
10–15 minutes
to the summit.
From the jump-off, the hanging bridge is about
30 minutes
downhill. Lion House Falls and a natural pool follow along the river, but the climb back up is the hardest part.
You can pitch a tent near the summit and in the campsite, and there are also roofed huts (kubo). It is close to the city, yet the night sky is relatively good.

items.title: Early-morning day route
items.subtitle: Sunrise and the Camp A ridge walk

children.text: Leave Cubao in Manila. If you drive, use Marcos Highway or C-6.
Arrive at the Fresno campsite entrance, register with your ID, sign the liability waiver, and get a guide assigned. Bring your own pen.
Switch on your headlamp and start up the ridge. The way to the summit is a gentle grassy path.
Wait for the sunrise and sea of clouds near Noah's Ark. On weekends there is a photo queue, so claim your spot early.
Visit Sambong Peak and the Spider Web viewpoint in turn.
Rest at the summit shelter, then head back to the jump-off for breakfast.
Camp A alone usually ends by mid-morning. If you still have energy by then, you can continue on the Camp B route.

items.title: Camp A+B full route
items.subtitle: From the ridge to the hanging bridge and the falls

children.text: After finishing Camp A, head down toward Camp B with your guide.
Walk the downhill trail for about
30 minutes
and cross the hanging bridge. It is high and you will feel it sway.
Use your hands to cross the rocky path along the river and continue toward the falls.
Turn back and climb up. The ascent takes about
1–1.5 hours
and is the hardest part, so go slowly.
Wash up at the jump-off, have lunch, and start heading home around
The day after rain, the river trail can be dangerous, and guides sometimes close the Camp B route. Follow their instructions.

items.title: From Manila by jeepney and tricycle

children.text: From Cubao, take a jeepney or van toward Cogeo (Antipolo). One blog gives about
30 minutes
and a fare of about ₱50.
From Cogeo, take a jeepney to Sampaloc (Tanay) and get off at the Maysawa junction. It takes about
45 minutes–1 hour
and costs about ₱65.
From Maysawa, take a tricycle to the campsite registration area. One blog says about
and another says about
Because jeepneys may not run before dawn, many people hire a tuk-tuk (about
, for 3–4 people) from Cogeo to the registration area.
The first jeepneys are generally said to run from around
. To catch sunrise, sleep nearby the night before or use a tuk-tuk or a rental car.
From Marcos Highway or C-6, go via Sampaloc Road onto Marilaque Highway. It is said to take about
2.5–3 hours
from Manila.
The last
1.5 km
is unpaved. It gets muddy when it rains, so a higher-clearance vehicle is safer.
Several day-hike packages leave from Makati and Ortigas Center. Transport and a guide are often included, so check what the package covers.
The best period is November through February, during the northeast monsoon (Amihan). The air is cool and the skies are clear, so you have a good chance of seeing the sunrise and the sea of clouds.
In the rainy season from June to October, the red clay trail is very slippery and the access road turns muddy. When a typhoon is coming, the Camp B route becomes dangerous, so avoid it.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: The best time, with the best chance of sunrise and a sea of clouds. Very crowded around the New Year and on weekends.
The shadeless grassy ridge gets very hot and dusty. Hike at dawn to avoid the sun.
Mud, slippery clay trails, and typhoon risk. Avoid the days right after rain.

items.label: Entrance and environmental fee
items.note: Blogs quote anywhere from ₱150 to ₱300, and day and overnight rates differ.

items.label: Guide (required)
items.note: Per group of up to 5. For Camp A only or Camp B only, it is sometimes quoted at about ₱300.

items.label: Jeepney (Cubao to Cogeo to Sampaloc)
items.note: Per leg, based on one blog. Check the time of the first jeepney.

items.label: Tricycle (Maysawa to registration area)
items.note: Fare is per tricycle, not per passenger.

items.label: 4x4 jeep (return from Camp B)
items.note: Per person, one way or round trip.

items.label: Tent pitching and overnight entrance
items.note: If you bring your own tent. Tent and hut rentals are extra.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.
To stay overnight in the mountain, pitch a tent in the campsite or book a hut (kubo). Check-in is usually after
and check-out is between
and noon the next day. Huts are reported to start at about

for 2 to 4 people, with larger rooms in the ₱3,000 range, but these figures come from older blogs, so be sure to check current prices. Bookings are said to be made through the Fresno campsite's Facebook page. Cooking is said to be limited to butane stoves.

A small store near the registration area sells snacks, coffee, and simple meals, but the choice is limited, so bring snacks and water. There are said to be country restaurants in Maysawa and nearby villages, including one with a view. Most people find lodging in Antipolo or in Tanay town. For an early-morning start, sleeping nearby the night before is much easier, and if you come as a day trip from Manila, plan your snacks and lunch in advance. After the hike, some places in Maysawa are said to serve ordinary Filipino home cooking (grilled pork, chicken, or vegetable dishes with rice) for around ₱120 a meal.
Before you leave, check the Fresno campsite's Facebook page and the Tanay municipal government's announcements. Access limits or fee changes are possible.
A guide is required beyond the summit. Each guide takes up to 5 people, so plan your group size accordingly.
Bring cash in small bills, a valid ID, and a ballpoint pen. Do not count on card payments or an ATM nearby.
Carry at least
of water per person. There is nowhere to buy water along the trail.
For a sunrise hike, prepare a headlamp, non-slip trail shoes, a hat, sunscreen, a rain poncho, a change of clothes, and a power bank.
On weekends the queues at Noah's Ark and the Spider Web get long. Weekdays are much more relaxed.
Smart mobile coverage is relatively good, but Globe is said to have dead spots. Tell someone your plans beforehand.
Carry out all your trash and do not pick flowers or plants. Bonfires and charcoal cooking at the summit are described as prohibited.
The red clay ridge is very slippery when wet, and the climb back from the Camp B river is hard on the knees. After heavy rain, postpone your trip.
The grassy ridge has almost no shade, so watch for heat stroke once the sun is up.
The hanging bridge and the Spider Web viewpoint are high, so do not push yourself if you are afraid of heights.
Pets are said to be prohibited. Do not bring a dog.
This is private land. Check on site whether it is open, the hours (roughly
to
), and the fees.
Late in the afternoon, jeepneys at Maysawa may be full or may stop running, so leave plenty of time to get home.
Pregnant women and people with heart, breathing, or mobility problems should avoid strenuous hiking.
A popular waterfall that many people combine with a trip to the Tanay area by car. Travel time varies with traffic, so check locally.
A scenic spot where wind turbines line a windy flat near the lake, and a frequent stop on Rizal day trips.

blocks.title: Tanay Old Town and San Ildefonso Church

children.text: After the hike, you can explore the historic church and old town in Tanay town.
A conservation area that requires advance booking, where you can enjoy another side of Rizal's mountain scenery after Mount Kulis. Check reservations and fees separately.
A rock formation on the Cuyambay side, mentioned as an additional trekking option close to Mount Kulis.
